la:verb:degusto.html:
dē-gusto, āvi, ātum, 1,
v. a., to taste, and thus diminish a thing (cf. delibo and ἀπογεύομαι—rare but class., esp. in the trop. sense).
Lit.: vinum,: pabulum,: novas fruges aut vina,: vasa vel dolia,.—
Poet. transf., of fire: ignes flammā degustant tigna trabesque,lick,. And of a weapon that slightly touches, grazes: (lancea) summum degustat volnere corpus,; imitated by .—
Trop.
To try, make trial of, make one's self acquainted with: eandem vitam,: literas primis labris,: aliquid speculae ex ejus sermone,: aliquid de fabulis,: genus hoc exercitationum, prooem. fin.: summatim ingenia maximorum virorum,: imperium,: istum convivam tuum,—
(Acc. to no. I. B.) To touch slightly upon, to treat briefly of: plures materiae inchoatae et quasi degustatae,: haec prooemio (opp. consumere),: genera (opp. excutere bibliothecas),.

la:adj:degener.html:
dē-gĕner, is (abl. degeneri, ), adj.
genus
,
that departs from its race or kind, degenerate, not genuine (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; esp. freq. in Plin. and Tac.; not in Quint. and Suet.).
Lit.: Neoptolemum,; cf. proles,; : dignitate formae haud degener,: hi (Galli) jam degeneres sunt, mixti, et Gallograeci vere, quod appellantur,; : canum degeneres,: aquila,: herbae,: adamantes,.—
With gen.: patrii non degener oris,; so, sanguinis,: patriae artis,: altae virtutis patrum,; .—
Transf., mentally or morally degenerate, ignoble, base: Muttinem sibi modum facere, degenerem Afrum!: Artabanum materna origine Arsacidem, cetera degenerem,; cf.: vitā non degener,: non degener ad pericula,: degeneres animos timor arguit,: animi,: metus,: questus,: preces,: projectus,: insidiae, et saep.—Of language: bilingues, paulatim a domestico externo sermone degeneres,.—Poet.: toga (for togati),.—With abl. ( = indignus): degener haud Gracchis consul,: tantoduce,.

la:verb:degenero.html:
dēgĕnĕro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.
[degener].
Neutr., to depart from its race or kind, to degenerate (class.).
Lit.: qui a vobis nihil degenerat,: Pandione nata, degeneras!: pomaque degenerant succos oblita priores,; cf. : frumenta,: surculus,: hordeum in avenam,; cf. : Macedones in Syros degenerarunt,; ; . —
Trop.
With ab: ab hac virtute majorum,; cf. ; so, a gravitate paterna,: a parentibus nostris,: a familia imperiosissima,: a civili more,: a fama vitaque sua,: non modo a libertate sed etiam a servitute,: a Stoicis degeneravit Panaetius,; cf. .—
With abl. alone: famā,.—
With dat. (poet.): degenerant nati patribus,; so, Marti paterno,: patri,.—
With ad or in and acc.: ad theatrales artes,: in feritatem,.—(ε) Absol.: consuetudo eum et disciplina degenerare non sineret,; : nec Narisci Quadive degenerant,; ; .
Act.
To cause to degenerate or deteriorate: Venus carpit corpus et vires animosque degenerat,: multum degenerat transcribentium fors varia,: ni degeneratum in aliis huic quoque decori offecisset,i. e. his degeneracy, his vicious character,; see Zumpt, Gram. § 638, N. 1.—
With acc. of that from which any thing degenerates, to dishonor, to stain, by degeneracy (poet., and in post-Aug. prose): non degenerasse propinquos (sc. me), (5, 1, 79 M): palmas,: famam,; . —Pass.: conspectus degenerati patris,; cf. .
la:verb:degenero.inflection: āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.

la:verb:dego.gloss: to pass time or spend time
senses: to pass time or spend time
la:verb:dego.html:
dēgo, dēgi, 3, v. a.
de-ago
,
to spend, pass, sc. time (for syn. cf.: ago, gero, facio—very freq. and class.).
With acc.: a mane ad noctem usque in foro dego diem,; so, diem in laetitia,: aetatem,; ; ; : omne tempus aetatis,: aevom,; ; ap. Augustin. Trin. 4, 2: vitam,; ; : quod reliquum est vitae,: senectam turpem,: otia pacato in thalamo, Catull. 68, 104 al.—Pass.: quantis periclis degitur hoc aevi,; so, aetas,; ; ; : vita,; —
Absol., to live (not freq. till after the Aug. period): laetus deget,: gentes sic degunt, prooem. § 1: certus procul urbe degere,: sine nequitia,; cf. ; : vita humanior sine sale non quit degere, to continue, endure, , § 88.—
To carry on, wage: nautae contractum cum ventis degere bellum (cf.: agere, peragere bellum),.!*? "DEGERE antiqui posuerunt pro exspectare," Paul. ex Müll.

la:verb:degero.html:
dē-gĕro, ĕre,
v. a., to carry away, carry off (rare): de vinea sarmenta, Schneid. N. cr.: mea ornamenta ad meretrices,: aurum meum tuae amicae, (, the true reading is digeritur).

la:verb:degredior.gloss: to go down, march down, descend
senses: to go down, march down, descend
la:verb:degredior.html:
dē-grĕdĭor, gressus, 3, v. dep.
gradior
,
to go down, march down, descend (never, to go away, depart, like digredior— freq. only after the Aug. period, esp. in Liv. and Tac.): de via in semitam, (dub.): degressus ex arce,: templo,: monte,: colle,: jugis,: Alpibus,fin.: palatio, al.—Absol.: degrediente eo magnā prosequentium multitudine,; ; ; ; : in campum,; fin.: in specum,: in aequum,: ad pedes,to alight, dismount,; . (In , the true reading is digredi.)
